children: A federal appeals court has denied a request by two parties that sought to block the Trump administration's plan to reschedule marijuana for medical purposes.

The motion from the National Drug and Alcohol Screening Association and MMJ International Holdings argued that marijuana abuse has consequences and providing tax benefits to cannabis companies will lead to more sales and abuse.
The Justice Department said in its brief that the attempt by challengers was from "pocketbook interests served by keeping all marijuana in Schedule I,"
An order signed in April by US Attorney General Todd Blanche would move medical marijuana from Schedule I to Schedule III under the Controlled Substances Act. It would also
licensed medical marijuana operators tax breaks and ease some barriers to researching cannabis.

title: Federal court allows Trump administration marijuana rescheduling to proceed
